processing_steps.atmosphere: vacuum induction melting under high purity Ar; as-cast ingot homogenized
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Ingot with nominal composition Fe-35Mn-6Al-0.1C-0.1Nb-0.1V-1Mo-1W (wt.%) was prepared by vacuum induction melting (50 kg) under high purity Ar atmosphere; the as-cast ingot was homogenized at 1150 °C for 4 h.
The homogenized ingot was hot-rolled (HR) into rods with a diameter of 16.5 mm.
The HR steel rods were solution-treated at 1050 °C for 2 h followed by oil quenching to obtain equiaxed grain structures with nearly equivalent grain sizes.

processing_steps.method: uniaxial tensile testing at liquid nitrogen temperature (LNT)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Standard tensile specimens with gauge length 25 mm and diameter 5 mm cut from the quenched rods with tensile axis parallel to the rod axis; tested at an initial strain rate of 1.0×10⁻³ s⁻¹ at LNT using an MTS tensile machine; at least three specimens deformed to fracture to confirm reproducibility.
Interrupted tensile tests to engineering strains of 3 %, 10 %, 20 %, 28 %, 38 % and 55 % were performed to reveal the microstructural evolution during straining at LNT.

structures.overall_structure: Solution-treated precursor (1050 °C, 2 h + oil quench): equiaxed FCC γ-austenite matrix with a small fraction (~3 vol.%) of BCC α ferrite uniformly distributed along austenite grain boundaries; abundant annealing twin boundaries (white lines); very weak texture; L1₂-type short-range ordering (SRO) and MC carbide present.
structures.number_of_phases: 2 (γ + α) plus MC carbide and L1₂-type SRO

phases_present.morphology: equiaxed matrix grains including many annealing twin boundaries
small particles uniformly distributed along the austenite grain boundaries

grain_structure.texture: very weak texture along the forging/rolling direction

precipitates.distribution: V fully dissolved in the steel; approximately 0.047 wt.% Nb, 0.017 wt.% Mo and 0.024 wt.% W existing in MC carbide
extremely weak superlattice spots near the [0-11] diffraction pattern; satellite reflections near some main γ spots

structures.overall_structure: LNT tensile deformation at 3 % engineering strain: complex planar slip features dominate; austenite remains stable.

defects.type: dislocation nodes, dislocation pairs and dislocation multi-junctions (complex planar slip)
stacking faults formed at annealed twin boundaries (low temperature facilitates planar glide)

precipitates.type: MC carbide particle at a {111}-faceted boundary

structures.overall_structure: LNT tensile deformation at 10 % engineering strain: pronounced complex planar slip together with deformation twins nucleated at annealed twin boundaries.

defects.type: deformation twins nucleated at annealed twin boundaries (related to stacking faults)

precipitates.distribution: fine parallel twin lamellae at annealed twin boundaries (width ~5 nm, below EBSD detection limit)

structures.overall_structure: LNT tensile deformation at 20 % engineering strain: dislocation cell blocks and dislocation cells develop; deformation twins present but proportion still very low (competition between dislocation gliding and twinning).

defects.type: dislocation cell blocks (in grains oriented away from <100>//TA) and dislocation cells (in grains close to <100>//TA)
deformation twins in grain interiors (low proportion)

precipitates.distribution: thin planar bands (width ~24 nm) in grain interiors

precipitates.type: cell blocks / dislocation cells (CBs or DCs)

structures.overall_structure: LNT tensile deformation at 28 % engineering strain: dislocation cell blocks refined; a small amount of wide and fine microbands; twins further activated but prevalence still relatively low.

defects.type: refined dislocation cell blocks and dislocation cells; microbands (plastic localization)

size.value: broad microbands ~390 nm; fine microbands ~137 nm

precipitates.distribution: broad microbands originate from grain boundaries; fine microbands originate within the grains

precipitates.type: cell blocks / dislocation cells (CBs or DCs)

structures.overall_structure: LNT tensile deformation at 38 % engineering strain: a significant number of deformation twins activated; denser, more diffuse high-KAM network than at RT.

phases_present.texture: <111>//TA texture strong (higher than at maximum uniform elongation at RT)

defects.type: dense deformation twins (dense parallel twin bundles) and dislocation substructure

precipitates.distribution: dense parallel twin bundles filling grains; type III grains form multiple-orientation twinning, type II grains single-orientation twinning

structures.overall_structure: LNT tensile deformation at 55 % engineering strain (close to maximum force strain): a large number of secondary twins activated in addition to primary twins; secondary twins contain more stacking faults than primary twins.

phases_present.morphology: primary twin bundles plus secondary twins rich in stacking faults

defects.type: primary deformation twins (further enhanced) and secondary deformation twins (significantly activated)
stacking faults (abundant in secondary twin lamellae)

size.value: average twin spacing l = 182 nm; average twin thickness e = 72 nm

precipitates.distribution: primary twins enhanced, secondary twins activated at 55 %, secondary twins contain more stacking faults

defect_interactions.interaction_type: twin boundaries act as effective barriers to dislocation motion
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Twin boundaries reduce the dislocation mean free path (dynamic Hall-Petch effect), contributing to the sustained hardening response in Stage D; at 55 % LNT the twin strengthening contribution is calculated to be 290 MPa (with l = 182 nm and e = 72 nm).

defect_interactions.interaction_type: stacking faults formed at annealed twin boundaries act as nucleation sites for deformation twins
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: At 3 % LNT distinct stacking faults form at the annealed twin boundaries; at 10 % pronounced deformation twins appear at the annealed twin boundaries as a result of the previously formed stacking faults.

defect_interactions.interaction_type: stress concentration at cell block walls with planar slip characteristics activates twinning
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Type II and III grains form cell block walls with planar slip characteristics producing stress concentration exceeding the macroscopic shear stress; the shear stress from this concentration significantly exceeds the macroscopic shear stress, activating twinning that macroscopically is unfavourable.

interfaces.slip_behavior: LNT deformation is dominated by planar slip (enhanced cross-slip at low carbon/high rate). Type II grains preferentially form single dislocation glide traces; type III grains tend to develop double glide traces; only a small fraction of type I grains exhibit slip traces and instead form uniform dislocation cells.
interfaces.phase_evolution: Austenite is highly stable; no phase transformation occurs in the austenite at LNT (γ fraction ~97 % stays essentially constant with strain), only BCC α phase present at a small fraction.
interfaces.interface_notes: In duplex steels the main crack sources originate from the FCC/BCC (γ/α) interfaces; for cryogenic impact samples fine cracks form around voids generated by detachment of α, indicating the γ/α interface serves as a crack initiation site, which may contribute to a decrease in crack propagation energy at low temperature.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: standard tensile specimen, gauge length 25 mm, diameter 5 mm
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: tensile axis direction parallel to the rod axis; LNT

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: LNT tensile engineering stress-strain curve (Fig. 2a) reaches just below 950 MPa and fails near engineering strain 0.75
strain_hardening_rate: LNT strain hardening behaviour divided into four stages (markers B, C0, C1, C, C2, D); hardening rate starts near 4000 MPa and falls step-wise to about 1500 MPa, staying well above the RT curve

Stage B: nearly constant high hardening rate (attributed to activation of twins at annealed twin boundaries); Stage C: continuous decrease (refinement of dislocation substructure); Stage D: sustained/constant hardening from extensive primary and secondary twinning

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: dislocation and twin strengthening contributions to flow stress at LNT

strain_hardening_rate: σ_dis(γ) (LNT): 58, 240, 379, 469, 504, 646 MPa at engineering strains 3.0, 10.0, 20.0, 28.0, 38.0, 55.0 %; σ_dis(α) (LNT-GND): 2, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9 MPa; σ_twin(γ) (LNT): 290 MPa only at 55.0 % engineering strain

comparative_performance.improvement_percentage: nearly 3 times higher than that of the 9Ni-steel

comparative_performance.benchmark_sample_id: high carbon lightweight steel; TWIP steel; low-carbon high manganese steel; 304 stainless steel; Al0.1CoCrFeNi HEA
comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Charpy impact energy and specific yield strength at LNT

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: JSM-7800 F SEM; raw EBSD data analysed with HKL Channel 5; step sizes of 1 μm, 300 nm, 100 nm and 30 nm
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: LNT tensile specimens at engineering strains 3 %, 10 %, 28 % and 55 %; IPF maps along the tensile axis (TA)
characterization_methods.purpose: reveal phases, grain size, dislocation (KAM/GND), texture and deformation twinning evolution during LNT tensile deformation
characterization_methods.key_findings: A weak initial texture strengthens with strain; strong <111>//TA and weak <100>//TA textures at LNT; twinning is orientation-dependent (type II and III grains); deformation twinning fraction increases with strain at LNT; no phase transformation.

characterization_methods.technique: transmission electron microscopy (bright-field, SAED, lattice imaging)
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: FEI-Tecnai G2 F20 operated at 200 kV
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: LNT tensile specimens at 3, 10, 20, 28, 38 and 55 % engineering strain
characterization_methods.purpose: investigate deformation substructures (dislocations, cell blocks/cells, microbands, stacking faults and deformation twins) at LNT
characterization_methods.key_findings: Planar slip at 3 %; deformation twins nucleated at annealed twin boundaries at 10 % (twin width ~5 nm); cell blocks/cells and twins at 20 % (twin width ~24 nm); refined substructure with microbands (390 nm and 137 nm) and twins (157 nm) at 28 %; abundant twins at 38 %; primary + secondary twins at 55 %.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: LNT tensile specimens at 0 %, 3 %, 10 %, 28 % and 55 % (phase fraction); Williamson–Hall analysis of (111)γ, (200) and (220) peaks for dislocation density
characterization_methods.purpose: determine phase fraction (austenite stability) and estimate dislocation density after different LNT tensile strains
characterization_methods.key_findings: Austenite fraction stays essentially constant (~95.6–97.3 %) with strain at LNT; the residual ferrite (110)α signal almost disappears away from 0 %; LNT total dislocation density rises from 0.72 to 13.32×10¹⁴ m⁻².

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: standard tensile specimens (gauge length 25 mm, diameter 5 mm), initial strain rate 1.0×10⁻³ s⁻¹, at LNT; interrupted tests at 3, 10, 20, 28, 38 and 55 % engineering strain
characterization_methods.purpose: measure tensile stress-strain responses and corresponding strain hardening rates of the LNT specimen
characterization_methods.key_findings: YS 497 MPa, UTS 945 MPa, uniform elongation 56.0 %, total elongation 75.5 % at LNT; four-stage strain hardening behaviour at LNT.

computational_details.simulation_method: thermodynamic calculation of stacking fault energy (γ_SFE) and γ→ε Gibbs energy difference (ΔG^{γ→ε})
computational_details.potential_model_or_database: Fe-Mn-Al-C approximate solid-solution thermodynamic model (Eqs. 3–8), including magnetic Gibbs energy term
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: test temperature T = 293 K (RT) or 77 K (LNT)

analytical_models.model_note: Calculated γ_SFE and ΔG^{γ→ε} at RT and LNT (Table 4); both decrease on cooling; SFE values are above the 20–45 mJ·m⁻² twinning window, contradicting observed twinning.

computational_details.simulation_method: critical twinning stress calculation (mean-field model and Hall-Petch-type relation)
computational_details.potential_model_or_database: mean-field twin nucleation model (Eq. 9) and Hall-Petch-type relation (Eq. 10)
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: G = 68 GPa; partial Burgers vector b = 0.147 nm; grain size D ≈ 10.8 μm; m = 0.326; K = 0.350 MPa·m^0.5
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Experimental critical twinning stress ~778 MPa at LNT is close to the Sachs (M = 2.2) model prediction (742 MPa).

analytical_models.model_note: Estimated stresses at LNT are lower than at RT, while the experimental critical twinning stress rises from 723 MPa (RT) to 778 MPa (LNT).

computational_details.simulation_method: flow-stress decomposition modelling by summing strengthening contributions (ferrite + austenite)
computational_details.potential_model_or_database: flow stress model Eqs. 12–19 (Hall-Petch grain-boundary strengthening, lattice friction, dislocation (Taylor) hardening and twin strengthening)
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: ferrite content ~3 %; austenite M = 3.06, α = 0.4, G = 68 GPa, b = 0.26 nm; ferrite M = 2.8, α = 0.2, G = 80.7 GPa, b = 0.248 nm; K_GB(γ) = 0.350 MPa·m^0.5; l = 182 nm, e = 72 nm at 55 % LNT
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Calculated contributions of dislocations and twins to flow stress are in excellent agreement with measured values (Fig. 13).

analytical_models.model_note: α was chosen as 0.4 based on the smallest σ_diff (Table 7); twin strengthening is significant only at high strain at LNT.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: molar fraction of phases versus temperature 950–1200 °C
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Phase diagram shows a small fraction of BCC phase, consistent with the XRD result of ~97 % austenite.

unmapped_findings: Charpy V-notch (CVN) impact energy of the alloy at LNT is 254 ± 6 J (RT 331 ± 4 J); this value belongs to the separate Charpy impact specimen (55 mm × 10 mm × 10 mm, V-notch depth 2 mm) rather than to the LNT tensile specimen.
Reduction of area of the alloy at LNT is 80 ± 1 % (RT 78 ± 0.5 %) from Table 2.

The LNT impact energy decreases about 30 % from 331 J (RT) to 254 J (LNT), attributed to the existence of 3.0 % α-phase in the austenite matrix; fine cracks form around voids generated by detachment of α (the γ/α interface serves as crack initiation site). Crack initiation energy Wm ≈ 80–100 J for both temperatures, propagation energy Wp drops from 251 J (RT) to 156 J (LNT).

Measured composition of the solution-treated specimen by wet-chemical analysis (wt.%): Mn 35.14, Al 5.97, C 0.095, Nb 0.11, V 0.10, Mo 1.24, W 0.95, Fe Bal.; austenite (γ): Mn 35.92, Al 5.88, C 0.098, Nb 0.09, V 0.09, Mo 1.12, W 0.86; ferrite (α): Mn 32.44, Al 6.83, C '–', Nb 0.09, V 0.18, Mo 1.54, W 1.63.
Density of the investigated steel measured using the principle of Archimedes is 7.18 g·cm⁻³.

Based on electrolytic extraction, V is completely dissolved in the steel while Nb, Mo and W are partially dissolved, with approximately 0.047 wt.% Nb, 0.017 wt.% Mo and 0.024 wt.% W existing in MC carbide.

Deformation twinning nucleates at about 10 % tensile strain at LNT, whereas at RT it occurs at about 28 % tensile strain, indicating strong dependence of twinning on both deformation strain and temperature.
RT (sibling) values for context: YS 251 ± 3 MPa, UTS 580 ± 6 MPa, uniform elongation 38.5 ± 0.5 %, total elongation 52.0 ± 0.5 %, RT true stresses 339/483/635/723/800 MPa at 3/10/20/28/38 % strain.
